verdict.rationale: Muse offers permission-based access control (approval cards, 'secure storage for your credentials', user-defined access to linked services, activity/permission logs) which implies some granular control over what an agent can touch, but there is no evidence of a true scoped/least-privilege API-credential issuance mechanism (e.g., generating limited-scope API keys or tokens for the agent) as opposed to consumer-style connect/approve toggles. Missing for 10: explicit scoped API key/token generation, granular permission scopes per credential, developer-facing credential management, and any third-party confirmation that access is truly least-privilege.
